newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritanian copper mine to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Mauritanian copper mine to go ahead.

text.p: Mauritanian and North American mining firm Societe Guelb Moghrein d'Akjoujt (GEMAX) plans to develop a copper deposit 260 km north of the capital Nouakchott following a feasibility study, a government statement said.
The mine, Guelb Moghrein d'Akjoujt, would produce 360,000 tonnes of cathode copper, 29 tonnes of gold and 2,000 tonnes of cobalt from known ores totalling 23.7 million tonnes, it said.

GEMAX, owned by equal 50 percent shareholders Societe Arabe des Mines de l'Inchiri (SAMI) and North American-based General Gold International S.A., would achieve a total turnover during the 14-year project of $1.175 billion, with provisional industrial and commercial profits of around $180 million.
The government would receive payments equal to 2.2 percent of turnover, 25 percent of industrial and commercial profits, and taxes on 20 percent of expatriate pay packages.
Management jobs would be passed over to local hire after three to five years and provision made for technology transfer to Mauritania.
Profits of around $19 million would be repatriated, the statement said.
In March Australia-based General Gold Resources NL signed a letter of agreement to sell its Mauritanian copper and gold mine assets to Canada's Solomon Resources Ltd.
The assets included a 50 percent stake in the Guelb Mogrhein project.
